trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: reference hedged net
trials.hypothesis: This is the world-2 reference unchanged: mask under 4 layouts in, 4 re-laid output maps summed. It sets the baseline for the round. If the world misaligns the layout of the mask, actions or obs in one of those 4 ways, it should score above 0. A 0 here, while wider hedges score, would show the deviation lies outside these 4 layouts.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: 16-layout wide hedge
trials.hypothesis: Hedges all 8 grid symmetries times type-major and type-minor action order (16 layouts), on both the mask inputs and the summed output maps. It targets any mismatch between the action layout and the obs frame that the 4-layout reference misses, for example a rotation or type-minor order. It is refuted if it scores 0 while the reference scores 0 too, or if it scores no better than the reference.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: reference with 5x5 head
trials.hypothesis: Same as the reference, but the head conv is 5x5 instead of 3x3. Each placement logit then sees a radius-2 neighbourhood, which hedges footprints larger than stated and anchors other than top-left (centre or bottom-right) that a 3x3 view may not cover after re-layout. It is refuted if it scores no better than the reference within noise (about 0.07).

trials.label: r1c4
trials.name: DONE-index hedge
trials.hypothesis: Bets that DONE may sit at index 0, which would shift every placement index by one. Two hedged groups are summed: one reads the mask as [place..., DONE], the other as [DONE, place...]. Each group has 4 layouts, its own output maps and its own DONE logit. If DONE is first, only this net can align its logits with the actions. It is refuted if it scores 0 while it trains no better than the reference.

trials.label: r1c5
trials.name: obs-frame hedge
trials.hypothesis: Bets that the obs grid is transposed or flipped relative to the mask and actions. The obs enters under 4 frames (as is, transposed if square, y-flip, x-flip), alongside the reference's 4 mask layouts and 4 summed output layouts. If the obs and mask frames differ, the reference's 3x3 convs mix cells that do not line up, and here the 1x1 stem can choose the matching obs frame. It is refuted if it does no better than the reference.

trials.label: r1c6
trials.name: combined hedge: 16 layouts, obs frames, 5x5
trials.hypothesis: Combines three hedges: 16 mask and output layouts, 4 obs frames and a 5x5 head (r about 1.5, so fewer steps). It covers layout, frame and anchor deviations at once. If it scores while the single hedges do not, two deviations act together. If it scores 0 while a single hedge scores, the cost of hedging everything outweighs the gain.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: 5x5 head, 1 PPO epoch
trials.hypothesis: This refines the only nonzero training signal (r1c3) with one change: 1 PPO epoch instead of 2. That gives about 300k samples instead of 172k at the same compute. If the 5x5 net is short of samples, not wrongly structured, its training success should rise clearly above 0.0006 and dev success above 0. Zero training success refutes this and suggests the 0.0006 was noise.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: 5x5 head, dilated second res conv
trials.hypothesis: This is r1c3 with the second residual 3x3 conv dilated by 2. The FLOPs are the same, and the receptive field grows from about ±4 to ±5 cells, with sparser long-range taps. It targets anchors or footprints offset several cells from the obs frame, or a shift between obs and actions, which the 5x5 head only partly covered. It is refuted if training success stays at or below r1c3's 0.0006 and dev success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: 5x5 head + global context
trials.hypothesis: This is r1c3, but a Linear projection of the pooled global features (mean and max) is added to every cell of the head before its ReLU, at full scale and with default init. Every placement logit can then use board-wide state, such as how far the build has progressed or non-local dynamics. It targets a world whose rules need more than local information. It is refuted if it trains no better than r1c3 (0.0006) and dev success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c4
trials.name: 5x5 head + dense remap branch
trials.hypothesis: This is r1c3 plus a dense branch: a 1x1 conv to 4 maps, flattened, then a default-init Linear to all placement logits. Its output is summed at full scale with the conv head, never gated or zero-initialised. It hedges an arbitrary fixed permutation or offset of action indices, which no symmetry hedge covers, and costs about 2% more FLOPs. It is refuted if it trains no better than r1c3 and dev success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c5
trials.name: 5x5 head, longer horizon
trials.hypothesis: This is r1c3 with gamma raised from 0.9 to 0.98 and gae_lambda from 0.85 to 0.9. With gamma 0.9, the +1 exact-build bonus at the end of a 10-30 step episode is discounted to 0.04-0.35, so the agent may learn to fill cells without learning to finish exactly. This is the horizon refinement the program allows once training success is nonzero. It is refuted if training success stays at or below 0.0006.

trials.label: r2c6
trials.name: 5x5 combined: dilation, context, dense, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: This combines the round's single changes: 5x5 head, dilated second residual conv, global context in the head, the dense remap branch and 1 PPO epoch (about 290k samples). If the deviation needs several of these at once, or the gains are small and add up, only this net may escape zero. If it scores 0 while a single-change candidate scores, the combination costs more than it gains. If everything scores 0, all these bottlenecks are refuted.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: obs memory-layout hedge, 5x5 head
trials.hypothesis: The obs may be stored channel-minor (Y,X,C) or (X,Y,C) and then reshaped to (C,Y,X), which scrambles cells across channels. No frame flip can undo that. Here the stem reads the obs under three memory layouts (CYX, YXC, XYC), with the reference's 4 mask and output layouts and a 5x5 head. Refuted if training and dev success stay at 0.

trials.label: r3c2
trials.name: obs memory-layout hedge, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: The same net as the obs memory-layout hedge, with one change: 1 PPO epoch, 256 envs and 16 minibatches, giving about 290k samples instead of about 170k. If the channel-minor obs is the deviation, the extra samples should lift training success clearly above 0. If the first candidate scores and this one beats it by more than 0.07, samples are the bottleneck. Refuted if both stay at 0.

trials.label: r3c3
trials.name: dense obs and mask embeddings
trials.hypothesis: Bets on an arbitrary fixed scramble of the obs or mask cells that no symmetry or memory-layout read covers. Default-init Linear layers map the whole flattened obs (to 4 maps) and the whole mask (to 4 maps) onto the grid. Their outputs join the reference's direct inputs in the stem at full scale, with no gate. The head is 3x3, so r is about 1.2. Refuted if it stays at 0 while it trains no better than the reference.

trials.label: r3c4
trials.name: full dihedral obs+mask+output hedge
trials.hypothesis: r1c5 hedged only the transpose, y-flip and x-flip of the obs. Here the obs enters under all 8 grid symmetries, concatenated into the 1x1 stem, so the stem can pair build channels with target channels rotated by 90 or 180 degrees. The mask and the output maps also get all 8 type-major symmetries. This targets a rotation between the obs (or channel groups) and the action frame. Refuted if it stays at 0.

trials.label: r3c5
trials.name: layer-shared encoder for dynamics
trials.hypothesis: Bets on changed dynamics, such as other drop rules or brick heights, that need layer-by-layer reasoning the flat 1x1 stem learns slowly. One 3x3 conv, shared across layers, reads each layer together with the layers above and below (build, target, missing and extra), plus heights and a z-coordinate. Its per-layer features join the reference inputs in the stem. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

trials.label: r3c6
trials.name: obs memory-layout + 16 action layouts
trials.hypothesis: Bets that the world stores everything channel-last: the obs as (Y,X,C) and the actions type-minor. Neither alone was tested together with the other. The three obs memory-layout reads are combined with all 16 mask and output layouts, using a 3x3 head to keep r near 1.15. Refuted if it stays at 0. If it scores while the 5x5 memory-layout candidate does not, the action order matters too.

trials.label: r4c1
trials.name: reversed-index hedge (DONE-first x 16 layouts)
trials.hypothesis: Bets that the action index is reversed or offset: DONE at index 0 and placements in reverse order, which equals DONE first plus a 180° turn. r1c4 hedged DONE first with only 4 layouts, so the reversal was never tested. Two groups (DONE last and DONE first) each get all 16 layouts on the mask inputs and the output maps, summed at full scale. Refuted if dev and training success stay at 0.

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: valid-anchor action enumeration hedge
trials.hypothesis: Bets that actions number only the valid anchors of each brick type, so each type's rows are X-dx+1 wide, not X. No symmetry hedge can undo that. Constant index tables gather the mask into (type, y, x) maps and scatter the output maps back to actions under two variants: blocks of size Y*X, and contiguous blocks. These sit beside the reference's 4 layouts, all summed at full scale. Refuted if dev and training success stay at 0.

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: decoupled critic (reward-scale hedge)
trials.hypothesis: Bets that the reward is on a different scale than described, so value-loss gradients swamp the shared trunk and the global clip of 1.0 shrinks the policy update. The critic gets its own small conv trunk on detached features, and its gradient is scaled by 0.1 through a detach trick. Adam's per-parameter normalisation keeps the critic learning at about the same speed. Otherwise this is the reference. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c4
trials.name: scale-normalised stem (obs-scale hedge)
trials.hypothesis: Bets that the obs values are on an unexpected scale or sign, for example unnormalised heights or 0-255 values. That would saturate the stem and make the initial policy nearly deterministic, so it never explores. The obs and the mask each pass through their own 1x1 conv and then GroupNorm before being summed, and GroupNorm also follows the second stem conv. The scale of the obs then no longer matters, and the mask keeps an equal voice. Otherwise this is the reference. Refuted if training success stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c5
trials.name: all new hedges combined
trials.hypothesis: Combines this round's four bets in one net: DONE last and DONE first, each with 16 symmetric layouts plus 2 valid-anchor enumerations; a normalised stem; and a decoupled critic with scaled gradient. r is about 1.35, so it trains on about 180k steps. If it scores while the single bets do not, two deviations act together. If it scores 0 while a single bet scores, the extra hedges cost more than they gain. Refuted if everything stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c6
trials.name: all hedges combined, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: The same combined net with one recipe change: 1 PPO epoch, 256 envs, 16 minibatches, entropy 0.005, gamma 0.95 and lambda 0.9. That gives about 315k samples instead of about 180k, plus more exploration. The wide hedge splits gradient across 36 layouts and may need more samples to lock onto the right one. If this scores and the 2-epoch version does not, samples were the bottleneck. Refuted if both stay at 0.

analyses.1: No trials have run yet, so no deviation is ruled out. The starting net scored 0 here. In 6 of 7 earlier worlds every trial scored 0, so this world probably differs from its description. Only the layout-hedged reference net ever scored (about 0.22, world 2). Round 1 therefore follows the program: the reference net, then single-change hedges that each target one possible deviation (action layout and symmetry, footprint or anchor reach, DONE index, obs frame), plus a combined hedge. One planned bet is replaced. Reordering the obs channels cannot matter to a net whose first layer is a 1x1 conv over all channels, so that slot tests obs-frame variants instead. Every file sets K = n_place/(Y·X) instead of assuming n_types. This hedges an action space with extra dimensions, such as a layer index. If n_place is not divisible by Y·X, each file falls back to a learned Linear embedding of the mask. All candidates use the reference recipe.
analyses.2: Every round-1 trial scored 0 on dev. The one nonzero training success was the 5x5 head (0.0006, about one episode), so it is the only lead and may be noise. These deviations are ruled out: (1) the 8 grid symmetries of the action layout, with type-major or type-minor order (r1c2); (2) DONE placed first (r1c4); (3) the whole obs transposed or flipped (r1c5); (4) obs channel order, which the 1x1 stem can learn. The parameter counts also show Z=6, n_types=4 and n_place divisible by Y·X, so the reshape path was used and compact indexing is ruled out. Still possible: anchor or footprint offsets wider than a 3x3 view, dynamics that need non-local information, an arbitrary permutation of action indices, a weak credit signal for the +1 exact-build bonus at gamma 0.9, and too few samples. Each candidate makes one change to the 5x5 net, except one that combines them.
analyses.3: After 12 trials, dev success is 0 everywhere. Training success is 0 too, apart from r1c3's 0.0006, which round 2 could not reproduce and is likely noise. These results rule out the following as the sole deviation: the 16 action layouts (8 symmetries times type-major or type-minor order); DONE at index 0; anchor or footprint offsets within about ±2 cells; whole-obs transpose and flips; a slow dense action remap; and the lack of global context, short horizon or too few samples. The 1x1 stem already learns any permutation of obs channels. So the untested deviations are: (1) the obs stored in a different memory layout, for example channel-minor (Y,X,C) read as (C,Y,X); (2) any fixed scramble of the obs or mask, which only dense embeddings can undo; (3) rotations of channel groups relative to each other, which needs the full 8-symmetry obs hedge; (4) dynamics that need layer-wise reasoning. This round tests (1)-(4), with one sample-count variant on the memory-layout bet.
analyses.4: After 18 trials every dev score is 0. Training success is 0 everywhere except r1c3 (0.0006), and its round-2 refinements also scored 0, so that was noise. Ruled out: the 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries, type-major or type-minor), DONE first with 4 layouts, flips, transposes and rotations of the obs or its channel groups, channel-last obs, small anchor offsets (5x5 head, dilated conv), global context, longer horizon, more samples (1 epoch), dense input scrambles and the layer-wise encoder. Since many 1x1 nets learn channel permutations, geometry is unlikely to be the problem. Three gaps remain. First, a fully reversed action index: DONE first plus a 180° turn, never tested together. Second, actions numbered only over valid anchors for each brick type. Third, an obs or reward scale that breaks training: a large value loss would dominate the gradient clip and the shared trunk. This last round tests each bet alone, then combined, with one combined net on a 1-epoch recipe.
